content.text:
I've submitted index 29 (In 0.18 / Sb 0.82) as the best composition, but all three measurements were near zero. That points to the whole In–Sb oxide line having almost no photoactivity at 2.4 eV, so I can't say for sure whether 29 is really the best in the library.

All three merit measurements are used; I used none of the XRD budget. For each point I picked a known phase that the models predict should absorb 2.4 eV light:

| Index | In / Sb | Target phase | Predicted gap | Stable? | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 0.80 / 0.20 | In11Sb3O24 | 1.9 eV | Yes | 9.6e-5 |
| 17 | 0.49 / 0.51 | InSbO4 | 2.2 eV | Yes | −6.6e-4 (no signal) |
| 29 | 0.18 / 0.82 | Sb6O13 | 2.05 eV | Not checked | **3.2e-4** |

- **Why these points:** the gaps are model predictions, and "stable" means the model placed the phase at zero energy above the convex hull. I skipped In3Sb5O12 because its predicted gap of 2.77 eV is too wide to absorb 2.4 eV light.
- **Why index 29 for the last shot:** it was the unexplored Sb-rich end, and the Gaussian-process suggestion tool also pointed there. With only two earlier data points, that suggestion carried little weight.
- **What wasn't confirmed:** without XRD I can't show that those phases actually formed at those compositions.
- **Untested:** the pure-In end (indices 0–6) and the middle of the Sb-rich range were not measured.
